use_case_summary: Velaris is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a customer-facing chat & document search product that mixes low-latency chat (99th <= 250ms token stream) with high-throughput batch embedding jobs. Primary asks: guaranteed sustained throughput for peak windows, predictable p95/p99 latency SLOs, and reserved GPU planning to avoid noisy-neighbor impact. Key constraints: VPC-only deployment, strict data residency (NA), SOC2/ISO27001 evidence, KMS integration for envelope encryption. They want a deterministic billing profile (committed monthly/annual) and an SLA that includes cross-region failover and explicit fallback behavior during saturation. SE recommendation is 8xA100 reserved, autoscale burst to compatible lower-cost variants for non-latency-sensitive batch, and KV/prefix caching to lower token load. Redwood must provide latency percentiles broken down by model variant, route policy examples for routing by latency vs cost, and documented cross-region failover playbook for DR tests.
reliability_and_fallback_notes: POC focus: reliability patterns for Dedicated. Discussed two-tier fallback: 1) within-region model variant fallback — prefer same-architecture quantized variant (e.g., 8-bit) with preserved API contract when primary is saturated; 2) cross-region failover policy — automatic slow-failover to secondary region with warm standby capacity for critical routes. Important: preserve user affinity for session-level KV cache; strategy: asynchronous cache replication + short TTL on cache keys to reduce correctness risk during failover. Also agreed on circuit-breaker thresholds: 85% GPU util sustained for 60s triggers partial degradation (route new sessions to variant), 95% sustained triggers cross-region spill with reduced token-limit per request. Ask from Velaris legal: define SLA credits tied to P99 latency and failover correctness window (time to restore session affinity). Operational runbooks must include traffic-shaping knobs, model-variant compatibility matrix, and rollback criteria for canary to full rollout. We noted trade-offs: region failover adds 150–300ms base RTT; therefore critical low-latency routes should have regional isolation + idle warm pool to meet p99 targets.
poC_and_capacity_plan: Proposed POC: 8x A100 (reserved) in primary NA region, 2x A100 warm in secondary region for failover. Autoscale policy: burst up to 50% extra capacity using committed burst pool; metric triggers: token-rate per-GPU, KV cache hit-rate below 60% -> scale up. Quantization plan: enable 8-bit variant for non-streaming batch embeddings and reranking; keep FP16 for chat stream. Expected monthly token baseline: ~1.8B tokens; peak concurrency modeling attached in drive doc. Need final signoff on commit length (12 vs 24 months) to finalize pricing and SLA uplift.
